toegepas.voor: Jy maak jou merk op jou stembriewe in 'n stemhokkie.
toegepas.na: Jy merk jou stembriewe in 'n stemhokkie.
toegepas.rede_vinder: One 'merk' on several ballots is a mismatch, and the plain verb says the same thing more directly.
toegepas.fout: One singular 'jou merk' spread over several ballots is a loose, English-shaped 'make your mark' where Afrikaans has the plain verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Jy merk jou stembriewe' is the natural Afrikaans phrase, matches the lesson's own stembrief and stemhokkie definitions, keeps the plural ballots and the place, and moves no meaning.

laat_vaar.blok: Jy stem nie self vir 'n President nie
laat_vaar.voor: Parlement wat die kiesers self kies
laat_vaar.na: Parlement wat deur die kiesers self gekies word
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: As written, 'wat die kiesers self kies' can also read as the part of Parliament that chooses the voters; the passive leaves only the intended reading.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: In context 'die kiesers self kies' reads only one way (the voters themselves choose, set against the President being chosen indirectly in the sentence before), the active form mirrors the decided Nasionale Vergadering definition, and the passive is longer and stiffer for a Grade 6 reader without being clearly better.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: kon nie die ander partye met genoeg steun uit die regering hou nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: kon nie die ander partye wat genoeg steun gehad het, uit die regering hou nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'met genoeg steun' can attach to 'uit die regering hou' (keep out by means of enough support); a relative clause ties it to the other parties and keeps the protected 'genoeg steun'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: In context 'partye met genoeg steun' reads as one noun phrase, matching the next sentence's 'Die kleiner partye met genoeg steun'; the relative clause breaks that parallel and lengthens a fact-checked sentence for no clear gain.
